newsitem.title: USA: Brady market continues lower with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Brady market continues lower with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Brady bond prices continued lower with U.S. Treasuries as market experts remained divided over whether the 25-basis point rate hike by the Federal Reserve Tuesday would negatively affect the fundamentals of emerging market countries and add to a widening of spreads.

"The external fundamantals are not particularly good right now and remember to some extent the external and internal fundamentals are not disconnected," said one fund manager at a major U.S. bank. "I would say we are in a period where riskier assets will underperform less risky assets and I think we will underperform Treasuries for awhile."
Market experts noted, however, that trading activity was extremely thin and is expected to remain that way ahead of the long Easter weekend.
At 1700 EST/2200 GMT, Argentine par bonds were 5/8 lower at 64-3/8 bid, Mexican pars were 1/2 weaker at 72-1/2 and Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/4 lower at 76-3/8 bid.

The fund manager, who requested anonymity, said the rate hike and the talk leading up to the Fed tightening basically spooked some of the crossover buyers who had been entering the market earlier this year in their search for yield.

"There are a lot of people for whom the emerging debt market is not in their index and so there has been a fair amount of crossover buyers retreating. I don't see anything that is dire here but I don't get a sense that we are through with a correction."
On Tuesday, the Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates 25 basis points to 5.50 percent.
Another market source said he did not believe that fundamentals of emerging market countries would be negatively impacted by the Fed's tightening move.

"We are likely to continue a period of volatility in the near term but on a fundamental basis I don't see how this tightening has significantly damaged the creditworthiness of some of the major countries."

"Overall, we are likely to have a market that will track very closely the long bond or the 10-year bond and then we expect to see a return by some serious money. I don't see much chances for widening," he added.
Among Eastern European instruments, experts said the market will be closely watching the strike in Russia.

"I think there is a lot of focus on the strike in Russia tomorrow. I think people are going to watch that very carefully," said Peter Allen, head of emerging market research at BankBoston. "It is a litmus test on the political effects of the problem with wage arrears."
Russian Vnesheconombank dollar loans fell 1-1/8 to 79-1/4 bid and the mark loans eased 1-7/8 to 83-5/8 bid.
